summary: Backend regression suite (pytest) run against Spring Boot TaxEdge API on external preview URL. 20/21 tests passed. All modules functional: auth+OTP stub, user profile, GST/ITR/TDS/Insurance/Loan CRUD with user isolation, Loan EMI computation, Loan status role guard, Document multipart upload+download+delete, Payment stub initiate+callback, Notifications role-guarded create+list+unread-count+mark-read, CORS preflight, duplicate email conflict. Only deviation: unauthenticated GET /api/users/me returns 403 instead of the specified 401.

minor.issue: Returns 403 Forbidden instead of 401 Unauthorized. This is Spring Security's default when no JWT is present. Spec requires 401. Fix: add a custom AuthenticationEntryPoint in SecurityConfig that returns 401 for missing/invalid credentials, distinct from 403 (access denied).

action_items: In /app/backend/src/main/java/com/taxedge/core/security/SecurityConfig.java (or JwtAuthFilter), configure an AuthenticationEntryPoint (e.g. new HttpStatusEntryPoint(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED)) so missing/invalid JWT results in 401, keeping 403 only for role failures.
critical_code_review_comments: Response envelope inconsistency: /auth/login and /auth/otp/send return LoginResponse directly while every other endpoint uses ApiResponse<{success,message,data,timestamp}>. Consider unifying.
OTP stub echoes the code as devOtp in the login response — good for dev but must be gated behind a profile/env flag before production.
AuthenticationEntryPoint missing → 403 for unauthenticated requests (see minor issue above).
PaymentService: /payments/callback has no signature/HMAC verification and accepts any transactionId+status. Acceptable for STUB but should reject spoofed callbacks in production.
GstReturnRequest uses periodMonth/periodYear (Integer) — should validate ranges (1-12 for month, sensible year bounds).
Document entity exposes 'originalName' while typical convention is 'originalFileName'/'fileName'; name it consistently across modules.
test_credentials: Random 10-digit mobiles per run; OTP always 123456. Admin role bumped via `mysql -uroot taxedge -e "UPDATE users SET role='ADMIN' WHERE mobile='<m>'"` then re-login to refresh JWT.
seed_data_creation: Each run creates 3 fresh users (regular, other, admin) plus one duplicate-email attempt user. No cleanup performed (would require admin delete endpoints).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v`. pytest.ini forces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`. Fixtures create users on-the-fly using random mobiles. /auth/register requires `mobile` in the body in addition to the Bearer token. GST/ITR/TDS/Loan DTOs each have specific required fields (see backend_test.py payloads). Loan uses 'amount' not 'principal'. Document response field is 'originalName'. Only known deviation: unauth /users/me returns 403 (Spring default) instead of 401.
rca of the issue: Unauthenticated 403 vs 401: Spring Security's default AccessDeniedHandler/AuthenticationEntryPoint chain returns 403 when the JwtAuthFilter finds no token and lets the FilterSecurityInterceptor reject. Root cause: SecurityConfig does not register an AuthenticationEntryPoint that emits 401 on missing credentials. Mitigation: `http.exceptionHandling(e -> e.authenticationEntryPoint(new HttpStatusEntryPoint(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED)))`.
